map.name: Original design (first drawings)
map.desc: The house as first drawn: 10x10 and 13x13 bedrooms, TV lounge with double height, terrace at the front.

doors.label: master bedroom door (3'-6" x 8' as drawn)

items.label: demo car (compact SUV, Daihatsu Rocky size)

critique.title: This bedroom has no window
critique.issue: Bedroom 10x10 (ground floor) has no outside wall, so it gets no daylight and no fresh air. It will feel like a store room and will need the AC all the time.
fixes: Swap the bedroom and the bathroom so the bedroom touches the back wall and gets a window
Make a small light shaft next to the side wall
At least add a high glass window to the dining + a fresh-air fan

critique.title: This bedroom has no window
critique.issue: Bedroom 10x10 (first floor) has the same problem: no outside wall, no daylight, no fresh air.
fixes: Add a skylight from the roof (the roof above is open)
Swap the bedroom and the bathroom
High glass window to the hall

critique.title: Kitchen has no window and no exhaust
critique.issue: The kitchen has no outside wall. Smoke and oil from cooking have nowhere to go, and a gas kitchen must have fresh air for safety. No exhaust pipe or shaft is shown.
fixes: Make an exhaust shaft in the kitchen corner up to the roof
Strong hood + exhaust fan + gas leak alarm
Or move the kitchen to the back or front where it can have a window

critique.title: Cooking smell goes everywhere
critique.issue: The kitchen is fully open to the TV lounge, and the lounge is open up to the first floor. Smell and noise will reach the bedrooms upstairs.
fixes: Glass sliding door between kitchen and lounge
Keep bedroom doors closed
Hood with a pipe to the outside

critique.title: Only one way into the kitchen
critique.issue: The counter closes the kitchen. You can only enter from the lounge side, right where the fridge door opens. Two people cannot pass.
fixes: Make the counter 2' shorter
Fridge that opens the other way

critique.title: Main electric board is inside the kitchen
critique.issue: The main board is on the kitchen wall above the fridge. Heat and steam are bad for it, and in an emergency you must reach over the fridge.
fixes: Move the board near the main door
Keep 3' free space in front of it

critique.title: Master bedroom door is under the stair landing
critique.issue: The door is drawn 8' high, but the stair landing is right in front of it. Its top part is hidden behind the landing, and you walk under the stair to enter the main bedroom.
fixes: Make the door 7' high
Move the door to the left on the same wall
Turn the stair so the landing is in another corner

critique.title: Stair step count does not match
critique.issue: The stair sheet says each step is 7.57" high. At that height step 19 already reaches the first floor, but the plan shows 20 steps. Different step heights make people trip.
fixes: Measure the real floor height on site and divide it equally before casting
11" deep steps are more comfortable than 10"

critique.title: Top of the roof stair is too tight
critique.issue: From the last step to the wall there is only 1'-6". This narrow strip is also the only way into the rest of the stair room. You cannot carry anything, pass someone, or stand while opening the door. The roof plan shows more space, but with these step sizes the stair needs more length - the drawing does not add up.
fixes: Put the roof door on the long side wall
Make the stair room 2' longer towards the front
Change the roof stair to a U-shape
(Not good) smaller steps - too steep

critique.title: Last step to the roof is only 3" high
critique.issue: The roof is 11' above the first floor. With 7.57" steps the last step is only 3.3" high. An odd last step is easy to trip on, especially in the dark.
fixes: Use 18 equal steps of 7.33"
Or raise the roof door floor to match

critique.title: Stair has only one handrail
critique.issue: The railing is only on the open side; there is nothing to hold on the wall side. The stair is 3'-3" wide inside - tight for carrying a bed or sofa upstairs.
fixes: Add a wall handrail
Bring big furniture up through the first-floor terrace door

critique.title: Roof stair starts at the bedroom door
critique.issue: The first roof step is only 3" from the bedroom 10 door (first floor). You walk out of the room straight into a step.
fixes: Start the roof stair from the living room side
Move the bedroom door 1'-6" to the right

critique.title: You hit your head at the small kitchen counter
critique.issue: The roof stair goes over the small kitchen counter. At one end there is only 5'-1" of head space. A 6'-2" person cannot use most of it.
fixes: Keep the counter only under the high part (3-4')
Move the small kitchen to the living room wall

critique.title: Crowded spot at the top of the stair
critique.issue: The main stair, bedroom 13 door, bedroom 10 door and the roof stair all meet in a 4'-6" wide space. People and doors get in each other's way.
fixes: Pull bedroom 13's corner wall back or use a sliding door
Make the hall wider

critique.title: Bedroom 13 size label is wrong
critique.issue: The label says 13'x14'-6" but the measurements add up to 13'. At 14'-6" the room would sit over the stair - not possible. This model uses 13'. Ask the architect to correct it.
fixes: Change the label to 13'x13'

critique.title: Main door opens right into the family lounge
critique.issue: There is no entry hall. When the door is open, people outside see straight into the TV lounge. Guests and family meet in the same space, and there is no place for shoes.
fixes: Add a jaali screen or a small entry hall
Let guests use the drawing room door from the verandah

critique.title: Guest toilet door is outside
critique.issue: The guest toilet opens onto the porch. Guests in the drawing room must go outside to use it - at night, in rain, in front of the road. The toilet also faces its door.
fixes: Open the toilet from inside the drawing room
Turn the toilet so it does not face the door

critique.title: People walk through the sitting area
critique.issue: Both drawing room doors are on the same wall, so the path between them goes through the sofas. One sofa had to be made smaller.
fixes: Make the lounge door a sliding door
Put the sofas on the other side

critique.title: TV lounge is the corridor for the whole house
critique.issue: To reach the kitchen, dining, bedrooms or stairs you must walk through the TV area. Watching TV and walking around always clash.
fixes: Keep sofas on one side and a 3'-6" walkway on the other
Use the verandah side for daily entry from the car

critique.title: Sun shines on the TV in the morning
critique.issue: The TV faces the big east window, so morning sun reflects on the screen. The drawing room door is also right next to the TV.
fixes: Put the TV on the front wall
Add blinds to the window

critique.title: You can see into the master bedroom
critique.issue: The glass corner of the master bedroom faces the dining and lounge. From there you can see the bed.
fixes: Use frosted glass
Or a display shelf instead of glass
At least curtains

critique.title: Dining chairs block the bedroom door
critique.issue: The 6-seat dining table leaves only 1' between the chairs and the bedroom 10 door. A pulled-out chair blocks the door.
fixes: Use a 4-seat round table
Move the table 1'-6" away

critique.title: Bathroom is hard for elderly parents
critique.issue: The bathroom door is only 2'-6" wide - too narrow for a walker or wheelchair. The shower has a glass screen and nothing to hold on to.
fixes: 3' wide door
Flat shower floor with a seat
Grab bars at the toilet and shower

critique.title: Dressing room has no door
critique.issue: The dressing room opening has no door, so bathroom noise, steam and smell reach the bed, and the AC cools the bathroom too.
fixes: Add a sliding door

critique.title: Balcony is only 2' wide
critique.issue: The bedroom 12 balcony is 2' deep. You cannot put a chair there - it is only good for plants or the AC unit.
fixes: Make it 4' if society rules allow
Use the front terrace for sitting

critique.title: Bed almost blocks the balcony door
critique.issue: In the furniture drawing the bed leaves only 1'-9" to reach the balcony door. In this model the bed is moved back to keep a path.
fixes: Move the bed back (as here)
Or use a smaller bed

critique.title: Back of the first-floor living room is dark
critique.issue: The 31' long living room gets light only from the terrace door at the front. The back part (small kitchen, stair) is dark all day.
fixes: Skylight over the stair area
Glass in the stair room floor

critique.title: Roof bathroom and laundry are outside
critique.issue: To reach the roof bathroom or laundry you must walk across the open roof - hard in rain, summer heat or at night. The laundry has no door.
fixes: Roof cover from the stair room to the laundry
Door on the laundry
Or move the laundry to the first floor

critique.title: Stair room is bigger than needed
critique.issue: The roof stair room is 10'x15'-9" but the stair is only 3'-6" wide. Half of the room is empty.
fixes: Use the empty half as a store or laundry

critique.title: No water tank in the drawings
critique.issue: No water tank is shown anywhere. A 1000 gallon tank weighs about 4.5 tonnes when full - it must sit on columns, not just on a slab.
fixes: Put the tank on the stair room roof, over its walls
Plan the solar geyser and pump at the same time

critique.title: Front frame needs strong support
critique.issue: The tall 4' frame on the front starts above the railing and its long top part is held only at its ends. It needs a properly designed concrete or steel frame, or the tiles will crack.
fixes: Ask the structural engineer to design it as a steel box
Take its leg down to the terrace floor

critique.title: Bathroom above the TV lounge
critique.issue: The bedroom 12 bathroom sits over the TV lounge with no wall below. Its pipes run in the lounge ceiling - a leak would drip over the TV area. The wall above also needs a beam.
fixes: Waterproof the bathroom floor well and add a ceiling access panel
Beam under the bathroom walls

critique.title: Big holes in the floor next to each other
critique.issue: The double height opening and the stair opening are side by side. They need strong beams all around, and the stair landing's support is not drawn.
fixes: Beams around both openings
Beam for the landing into the side wall
Get the structure drawings checked

critique.title: We asked for full glass on the stair wall
critique.issue: We asked the designer for glass from top to bottom here, but the drawings show only three narrow glass strips. Turn on "Full glass on stair wall" in the menu to compare. Full glass needs a steel frame and protection from morning sun.
fixes: Steel frame with strong low-heat glass
Vertical fins outside to block morning sun

critique.title: Double height: heat, noise and cleaning
critique.issue: The 24' high space with east glass gets hot in the morning and is hard to cool. TV noise goes up to the bedrooms. The tall glass behind the stair cannot be cleaned from inside.
fixes: Low-heat glass + blinds
Big ceiling fan in the double height
Plan how to clean the glass from outside

critique.title: No covered parking, cars only one behind the other
critique.issue: There is no car porch. The 10' side strip fits two cars only one behind the other, and there is no rain cover between the car and the verandah.
fixes: Light steel roof over the side strip
Park the second car short of the verandah

critique.title: Back passage is only 2'-6" wide
critique.issue: All bathroom windows open onto a 2'-6" passage facing the neighbour's wall. Little light, little privacy, and it is the only way to the back for repairs.
fixes: Frosted top-hung windows
Keep the passage empty

showcase.title: Verandah and the 4' main double door
Double height, skylight and the stair-wall glass
Roof: stair room, skylight box, sitting area
The house at night - profile lighting on the elevation
